A1.justification: Both PDFs describe I-LLMRec despite the changed title and module names. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments, image-description similarity measurements, efficiency analyses and ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparator experiments, robustness analyses and catalog-scaling simulations.

M1.justification: The core adaptor, alignment and retrieval objectives, frozen LLM and score fusion remain unchanged; ILA and IRE become RISA and RERI. A limited input adaptation averages sampled-frame image features for MicroLens video recommendations (Appendix E.4).

E1.justification: v2 retains the original four Amazon categories and COCO similarity analysis, while adding Amazon Automotive, Video and Clothing, H&M Fashion, MicroLens and Goodbooks. It also evaluates entirely unseen target items and low-resolution images, substantially extending domains and test conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its comparator set. Appendix D.3 newly evaluates LC-Rec and IDGenRec on Sport and Art, broadening comparison to competing semantic-ID and textual-identifier representations. IDGenRec was discussed but not experimentally compared in v1.

E3.justification: The original leave-one-out protocol, 100 sampled negatives and Hit/NDCG metrics remain unchanged. New protocols include full-catalog comparisons, unseen-item subsets containing 302 Sport and 29 Art users, user-history grouping, extraction-inclusive timing, and 5K–20K catalog simulations with top-100 reranking. These are additions rather than demonstrated revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of entirely unseen items, cold/warm users, image-quality sensitivity, successful versus unsuccessful image cases, and expanding catalogs with model reuse. Existing module, LoRA, backbone and training-strategy ablations remain; the missing-image experiment moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix E.8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The additional results continue the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained tables preserve their numerical values, but v2 adds substantial new results. Examples include MicroLens Hit@5 of 0.4854 versus TALLRec's 0.4459 and Goodbooks Hit@5 of 0.4870 versus TRSR's 0.5100 (Tables 6–7). Full-catalog, robustness, timing and scaling outcomes are newly reported, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The original mathematical definitions, objectives and quadratic token-length complexity analysis remain equivalent. Appendix E.13 adds a limited complexity argument asserting O(1) visual-feature indexing and catalog-independent request cost under fixed top-100 reranking; no supporting proof is added.

C1.justification: The central efficiency, effectiveness and description-noise robustness contributions remain. The abstract narrows the empirical claim from outperforming existing methods generally to outperforming methods using textual descriptions for item representation on real-world Amazon datasets.

C2.justification: v2 explains the Goodbooks disadvantage through weak visual information, qualifies robustness under poor image quality, and hypothesizes why longer user histories hurt performance. Section 5 develops the interpretation of modality overlap as an efficiency advantage, while Appendix G expands v1's brief acknowledgment of missing text-specific information into a substantive limitation and research direction.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the adaptor's 512-unit intermediate dimension, offline feature caching, 3.4 KB per-item cache size, video-feature construction, and scaling-related memory, storage, throughput and training costs. The original learning rate, training batch size, hardware and code URL are retained; caching disclosure does not establish a changed original procedure.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through discussion of semantic IDs and textual identifiers, multimodal redundancy, and recent multimodal LLM recommenders such as MSRBench and MLLM-MSR (Section 5; Appendices D.3 and F). The earlier sequential-recommendation discussion is largely retained and relocated.

P1.justification: v2 renames the paper and modules, edits the introduction, merges training and inference sections, and moves implementation details, baseline descriptions, missing-image analysis and sequential related work into appendices. The appendices are extensively regrouped, with a contents page and dedicated discussion and limitations sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column ACM formatting to single-column ICLR formatting, with extensively resized and repositioned displays. v1 Figures 1–2 merge into v2 Figure 1; several retained multipanel plots are rearranged. New benchmark and image-quality tables and user-group and image-case figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's recommendation evidence centered on four Amazon categories and left visual-extraction costs unspecified. v2 addresses important gaps through competing compact-representation baselines, extraction-inclusive timing, and tests that expose applicability limits, especially TRSR's advantage on Goodbooks and sensitivity to poor images. These additions substantially strengthen empirical support and qualification without changing the retained results. Ambiguous timing wording between Section 4.3 and Appendix E.5 remains, but does not outweigh these gains.
